design.private_world_oracle: geometry-only cut drawn independently of every private transition
design.oracle_crossing: score only held-out species whose sampling geometry spans the oracle cut

interpretation.field_learning: The held-out scorer reaches the prospective 0.80 power floor when handed the true boundary (oracle-all). The learned training field is therefore the main power bottleneck in the current Queensland topology benchmark.
interpretation.observability: Restricting evaluation to species that geometrically span the oracle cut does not improve the worst-layout power (0.78 vs 0.80), so simple crossing-only filtering is not the primary remedy.
interpretation.null: Even a geometry-only oracle cut independent of private trait transitions produces 0.11-0.12 worst point rejection under the zero-centered species bootstrap. Coarse geography has non-zero chance commonness, so the sharedness null must condition on geometry rather than assume E[C_s]=0.
interpretation.next_step: Develop and calibrate a geometry-conditioned chance-commonness null on the frozen Queensland topology before changing the field learner or opening empirical DNA.
